content.text: {"answer":"No — that would revert exactly the issue d2 fixed. The recorded reasoning was explicit: returning the org-wide token means \"any authenticated user gets credentials for every machine in the org. That must end before a second user exists\" (m1812). The chosen design instead has the Worker mint an app-scoped, 1h-expiring deploy token via `createLimitedAccessToken` and hand only that to the CLI (packages/control-plane/src/fly.js:48-56), and the code's own header comment codifies the invariant: \"The org admin token (env.FLY_API_TOKEN) never leaves this process; the CLI only ever receives 1h app-scoped deploy tokens\" (fly.js:1-2). Falling back to the org token on a minting failure would violate that invariant and reintroduce the exact multi-tenant credential leak d2 was written to prevent.\n\nIf minting fails, the recorded design gives no sanctioned fallback to the org token — that path isn't documented anywhere in this snapshot. My advice: surface the mint failure as a hard error to the CLI (fail the deploy) rather than degrading security, and log/alert on it so it's investigated as a Fly API or auth-token problem (e.g., check the org token still supports `createLimitedAccessToken`, per d5's constraint that only Fly user auth tokens can mint scoped tokens).","citations":[{"kind":"decision","decision_id":"d2"},{"kind":"message","message_id":"m1812"},{"kind":"code","path":"packages/control-plane/src/fly.js","start_line":1,"end_line":2},{"kind":"code","path":"packages/control-plane/src/fly.js","start_line":48,"end_line":56},{"kind":"decision","decision_id":"d5"}]}
